A gate draft is authored text and must be treated as new. ⭐ THE REAL LESSON OF THIS FILE, AND IT IS THE ONE TO CARRY: ROUND 2's BREAKS WERE BOTH IN ROUND 1's FIXES. (a) Round 1 replaced a false assistant guarantee with a DIFFERENT false guarantee from the same retired list. editorial-standards.html's own stamp records apologia-argument removing three false guarantees from that page; round 1 removed guarantee #2 ('answers from our reviewed material') and installed guarantee #1 ('cannot be quoted' — a non-sequitur, because the model knows the Fathers independently of retrieval). It is false because api/ask.js:279 builds the sources block ONLY `if (hits.length)`, and retrieveSources returns [] below a score of 3 (lib/retrieve-sources.js:61) — measured at roughly two ordinary questions in three, including 'How do we know Jesus rose?' — so on most questions the system prompt carries NO patristic-quotation rule at all. FIXED by porting the construction claim from editorial-standards.html:135, which is true whether or not retrieval fires: 'the only such text placed in front of it is drawn from passages our citation check has already verified word-for-word'. (b) Round 1's 'renamed using our own nav label' swapped the NOUN and kept the certified number and predicate. There are not 156 Fathers and creeds: there are 156 PASSAGES across 41 distinct authors and councils (measured from sources-index.json), several of them neither Father nor creed (the Didache, the Epistle to Diognetus, the Book of Common Prayer, Perpetua). A Father is not checked word for word; a passage is. This is the documented 'a ported predicate detached from its qualifier is not a port' failure. FIXED by restoring the certified pairing from editorial-standards.html:118 and sources.html:193 — passages, checked word for word. Orthodoxy raised the same string as its round-2 [DRIFT] and as a clarifier candidate (a compressed viewer could read 'checked' as a claim about the TRUTH of the creeds rather than the accuracy of the quotation, a distinction api/ask.js:19 fences explicitly); the same rewrite discharges both, and no orthonote is owed because a reel frame cannot host one. ⚠ ROUND 2 ALSO CAUGHT A HALF-APPLIED FIX — the exact failure this repo keeps recording. Round 1 deleted 'the standard behind all of it' from the VOICEOVER and left the scene KICKER reading 'THE STANDARD BEHIND IT', whose 'IT' takes the same whole-feature-list antecedent, while the scene body underneath had been correctly narrowed to essays. Kicker now 'BEHIND EVERY ESSAY'. Clearing a claim from one surface is not clearing it from the scene. ⚠ 'ASK ANYTHING' RETIRED (orthodoxy [NOTE], denominational neutrality). A paid ad saying 'ask anything' invites a Catholic or Orthodox reader to test it with a Marian or Eucharist question and receive a decline, turning a principled neutrality commitment into an apparent evasion for exactly the readers that commitment protects. Do NOT 'recover' it with 'you will be carrying them' — that reopens the promise in plural form. ⭐ SCOPE DECISION UPHELD BY BOTH LENSES IN BOTH ROUNDS: 'Someone asked. / You froze.' is pastorally defensible — it names an experience without assigning fault, and scene 2 relocates the cause to preparation, which is what 1 Peter 3:15 commands. ⚠ DO NOT SOFTEN SCENE 2: 'you just were not carrying them' is the sentence doing all the tone work in the piece. Orthodoxy's round-1 [NOTE] applied: the exonerating sub-line was 'dim' at s=40 against a gold s=110 accusation, so on a silent scroll-past the un-shaming was the least visible thing on screen; promoted to cream, and the tense corrected to match the voiceover. ⚠ THE FIVE-STAGE CLAIM IS GONE AND MUST NOT COME BACK. voiceover: Someone asked. And you froze. Not because there is nothing to say. There are good answers — you just were not carrying them. That is what Apologia Daily is for. Ninety-two deep-dive essays across eight categories. A hundred and fifty-six passages from the creeds and the Fathers, each checked word for word. Ask the hard ones. It names its sources — and the only Fathers we put in front of it are already checked. Then you practise: a sparring partner, flashcards, and explain it back to get marked. Five minutes a day. One question, one argument — and it compounds. And every essay carries a dated record of the reviews it passed. So the next time someone asks, you will be ready. Apologia Daily. Start free.
